title: Anaesthesia of Lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) Fries
author: Julianne Valla Jacobsen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wg2fbye
materials: The following chemicals and concentrations were used in our study:Liquid Benzoak was stirred into seawater (12.5, 25, 37.5, 50, 100 mg/L), metacaine powder and the corresponding weight of sodium bicarbonate (Na2CO3) were dissolved in seawater at concentrations of 25, 38, 44, 60, 75, 100, and 150 mg/L. Isoeugenol (540 mg/ml) was diluted in ~5 mL heated (30oC) water prior to being added to the seawater to yield 6, 12.5, 18, 25, and 50 mg/L.

steps.title: Transfer fries to anesthetic box
steps.instruction: Move each individual lumpfish fry from the holding tank into an aerated transparent box of 5 L that already contains the pre‑mixed anesthetic chemicals.

steps.title: Determine induction time and SB concentration
steps.instruction: For a batch of 10 fries, record the time required to reach surgical anaesthesia (stage 3b, defined as immobile with weak respiration). Stop observing any fish that does not reach stage 3b within 10 min (600 s). Identify the chemical concentrations that achieve stage 3b in approximately 3–5 min; these are designated the Selected Best (SB) concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Observe each fry and note the time to stage 3b.
If stage 3b is not reached within 600 s, terminate observation for that fry.
Select concentrations that consistently induce stage 3b in ~3–5 min as SB concentrations.

steps.title: Test safety margin of SB concentration
steps.instruction: Expose batches of 10 fries to the SB anaesthetic concentration for three exposure periods: 5 min, 10 min, and 20 min.

substeps.instruction: Place a batch of 10 fries in the anesthetic box at the SB concentration for 5 min.
Remove the fries and proceed to the next batch.
Repeat the exposure with a new batch for 10 min.
Repeat the exposure with a new batch for 20 min.

steps.title: Transfer fries to seawater containers
steps.instruction: After exposure, move each fry to an individual container of approximately 1 L that contains only seawater.

steps.title: Measure full recovery time
steps.instruction: Record the time each fry takes to resume normal swimming (full recovery). End observation if a fry has not recovered within 15 min (900 s).

substeps.instruction: Observe each fry and note the time to normal swimming.
If recovery has not occurred by 900 s, terminate observation for that fry.
